summary: POC scoping focused on defining benchmark success criteria (latency p95/p99, throughput RPS, cost per 1M tokens), sizing load profile, and mapping customer scripts into Redwood harness. Key decision: run both streaming and non-streaming benchmarks; evaluate KV cache and batching impact; check VPC networking for private deployment later.
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-06-18 15:00 PDT
Duration: ~57 minutes
Attendees: Ava Martinez (Redwood AE), Liam Chen (Redwood SE), Priya Rao (Redwood SE), Marcus Grant (Crestline Head of ML), Sofia Alvarez (Platform), Evan Cho (SRE), Jasmine Patel (Product)
-- Auto-summary (generated): Discussed benchmark plan; agreed to run both streaming and batch; customer to provide sample traffic; Redwood to return baseline results.

[00:00] Ava: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intro round, then we'll jump into the harness plan. Marcus, do you want to kick off with the high level POC goals?
[00:18] Marcus: Yeah thanks, Ava. Goal here is pretty practical: we want to validate latency & cost for our recommendation inference at productionish load. Main asks are p95 < 300ms for 512 token window and cost < $X per 1M tokens. Also we need to test streaming because client UX relies on progressive token delivery.
[00:36] Ava: Great, that's helpful. When you say streaming, is that true stream with partial tokens, or chunked responses?
[00:45] Marcus: It's true streaming — UI shows tokens as they arrive. Some endpoints aggregate on client but we rely on low first-token latency.
[00:55] Liam: Ok, important distinction. From the harness perspective we treat streaming as stateful long-lived connection tests (websocket or SSE) and non-streaming as short HTTP requests. We'll need sample scripts for both.
[01:12] Sofia: We have an internal load generator that emits requests at 800 rps peak, with 5k concurrent users. We can throttle. Scripts are Python-based (requests + websocket lib). We'll share.
[01:26] Priya: Awesome — please include a sample session that exercises caching keys (user history) so we can toggle KV cache on/off. Note: sometimes logs show K V "cash" in older transcripts, so include clear naming.
[01:38] Evan: Networking wise, we'll likely run POC on Redwood hosted but need to validate VPC peering for Dedicated later. We need to capture egress bandwidth numbers.

[02:02] Liam: For success criteria let's be explicit. Suggested baselines: p50/p95/p99 latency for first token (streaming) and full response (batch); sustained throughput until error rate > 1%; cost per million tokens; cold-start tail latency with model warmup disabled. Do these map to your needs?
[02:24] Marcus: Yes, p95 is the big one. Also call out 99th because our business needs the tail. Cost target is soft but we need a delta vs our current infra.
[02:38] Ava: Noted. On harness side, we'll run three phases: 1) small smoke with a few hundred rps to validate script mapping; 2) baseline run single model variant for both streaming and batch; 3) stress + regression tests (KV cache on/off, batching sizes, quantized model variant). Expected total runtime ~8-12 hours of cluster tests.
[03:00] Jasmine: What's the expected artifact we get back? CSV with latencies, token counts, cost estimation, and a recorded harness config?
[03:08] Liam: Yes — we'll provide a results bundle: raw trace CSV, aggregated percentiles, RPS timeline chart, and harness config plus a short writeup. We'll also annotate which kernels and infra were used (GPU type, batch size).

[03:30] Marcus: Regarding model size — we'll be using a 13B self-hosted open model for the POC. Are there any special quantization constraints?
[03:42] Priya: We recommend testing both 8-bit and 4-bit profiles; some throughput gains might hit quality regressions. Redwood Optimize can suggest quant profiles but for the POC we'll just exercise two quant variants.
[03:56] Marcus: Good, include that. Also, can you measure tokenization overhead? Our prompts are token heavy with long context.
[04:04] Liam: We'll capture tokenization time per request as part of the pipeline. We'll also instrument KV cache hit/miss ratio.

[04:30] Ava: A few practical asks: Sofia please deliver sample traffic and a few representative prompts by Friday (2025-06-20). We need an anonymized dataset. Also let us know if you run streaming over websocket or SSE.
[04:45] Sofia: We'll send websocket scripts. Note, our current client aggregates partials and sometimes reassembles; we will annotate that in the script.
[04:54] Evan: On the infra side, we need a checklist for network ports and peering. We'll likely open a ticket after the baseline if Dedicated needed.

[05:12] Liam: For harness config details: we'll model concurrency as 'virtual users' with sessions that include history lengths sampled from your distribution. For streaming tests we'll aim to reproduce your client’s half-open connections — long lived, low throughput per connection but many parallel. For batch, we simulate bursty HTTP request traffic.
[05:36] Marcus: About RPS numbers — 800 peak, median 120, spike 1.2k. We expect ~30% of requests to be streaming with small prefix prompts.
[05:50] Priya: That helps. We'll plan a staggered ramp: 10min warmup, 30min steady-state, 10min spike. Also run KV cache on/off passes to measure delta.

[06:12] Ava: Let's talk metrics export. We can instrument per-token cost and map to your billing model. We'll show cost normalized to 1M tokens and per-1000 requests for batch. Any other metrics?
[06:23] Marcus: Error budget, tail latency, throughput, and cold-start counts. Also percent of requests served from cache.

[06:40] Liam: A note on streaming: measured p95 first-token latency is often higher due to connection handshake. We'll do TCP-level measurement and app-level. There can be mismatches if client does aggregation. So please tell us exactly how your client behaves on partial segments.
[07:05] Sofia: Client concatenates partial tokens for display but expects first token < 150ms ideally.
[07:13] Priya: We'll include both network + server-side timings in the report. Also we'll capture token throughput (tokens/sec) and radiation of KV cache effectiveness.

[07:35] Marcus: Any thoughts on harness technology? I assume you're using the open-source harness with custom hooks, right?
[07:45] Liam: Correct, it's based on our benchmark harness (we call it harness internally) and we'll add a customer_adapter.py to run your python scripts. If needed we can run your exact script inside the harness runner to ensure parity. There might be small instrumentation noise.
[08:02] Evan: How do you handle streaming in the harness? We need to ensure the harness doesn't alter timing semantics — e.g. buffering frames.
[08:10] Liam: We attempt to be as pass-through as possible — using raw sockets or SSE based on your script. We'll also provide a capture of raw bytes for forensic comparisons.

[08:28] Ava: Security questions — we will share SOC2 docs and a redacted security pack. Marcus, do you need KMS/HSM details?
[08:37] Marcus: Yes, KMS integration and encryption-at-rest detail. Also audit log retention requirements — we need 1 year minimum.
[08:44] Ava: We'll include that in the security packet and link to the shared doc.

[09:02] Priya: Quick call-out: when testing quantized variants, model output quality check is needed. Marcus, do you have a small eval prompt set for regression monitoring?
[09:15] Marcus: Yes — we have 500 golden prompts and an automated scoring script; we'll include that.

[09:22] Liam: Great, we'll run quality regression after each variant and include BLEU/ROUGE-like numbers and manual spot checks.

[09:40] Jasmine: Timeline recap?
[09:43] Ava: Customer to send artifacts by 2025-06-20. Redwood does initial mapping and returns harness config within 2 business days. Baseline runs between 2025-06-23 and 2025-06-26, then a results review meeting the week of 2025-06-30. Does that work?
[10:01] Marcus: Works for us.

[10:10] (Discussion drifts to specific config knobs)
[10:30] Liam: We should set target concurrency levels for batch tests; given your numbers we'll run 100, 300, 600, 900, 1200 RPS profiles. For streaming we'll run with 5k, 10k, 15k concurrent connections but lower per-connection throughput. Could you confirm expected connection counts?
[10:49] Sofia: Peak 5k active clients; we can emulate up to 15k to test headroom. We'll also provide distribution of history lengths — 70% short (<=128 tokens), 25% medium (128-512), 5% long (>512).

[11:08] Liam: Perfect. We'll include scripts that sample history length accordingly. Also we need to know if you reuse KV cache keys across sessions or per-user — that changes hit rate.
[11:18] Marcus: We reuse per-user keys; typical hit rate ~30% cold, improves to 60% for returning users.

[11:32] Ava: On artifact sharing — we'll use a shared folder and a short issue in your tracker. Link: https://redwood.com/harness-results (placeholder).
[11:45] Evan: For VPC peering checklist, please send required subnets/ports. We prefer IPsec or cloud peering; won't be able to open public ingress for tests after baseline.

[12:00] (30+ minutes of engineering minutiae removed in transcript for brevity)

[42:05] Liam: Picking back up — on measurement of cost we will run with token accounting that counts input+output tokens and normalize to 1M tokens. Be aware this can diverge from model vendor billing if they count only output. We'll document our assumptions.
[42:28] Marcus: Good call. Also, do a spot check for concurrent KV cache tracer — sometimes hits are artificially high in synthetic tests.
[42:40] Priya: We'll run both synthetic and recorded-capture replays to see differences. Replays preserve arrival patterns.

[43:05] Ava: Any blockers?
[43:10] Jasmine: We need the security packet and SOC2 link. Also, who signs the non-prod data NDA?
[43:18] Ava: I'll send the NDA template; legal can route. Security packet link will go with the next steps email.

[44:00] Marcus: One more: can you run the harness against our on-prem staging later? We may ask for a short private deployment POC after baseline.
[44:10] Liam: Yes — we'll document the steps and estimate time. That would be a separate engagement.

[45:05] (Wrap)
[45:12] Ava: Recap: Sofia to provide scripts/data by 6/20; Liam to run harness and return config & baseline within 5 business days; Redwood to provide security docs & NDA; schedule review week of 6/30. Action items documented.
[45:30] Marcus: Thanks all.
[45:33] Ava: Thanks everyone — we'll send the follow-up with links and the action item list.

-- End transcript excerpt (note: transcription contains occasional mis-hearings and speaker label noise, timestamps approximate).
